author: Milda 444
caption: The water surface curves down in the middle (the meniscus): read the scale at the bottom of the curve, with your eye level with it.

author: Al Riaz Uddin
caption: A stopwatch measures short times far more accurately than a wall clock; count what one small division on its dial is worth before you read it.

author: Scootdive
caption: Red blood cells, magnified thousands of times: these tiny disc-shaped cells carry oxygen around the body.

author: National Cancer Institute (NCI-Frederick)
caption: Blood contains different cells: a red blood cell (left) carries oxygen, and a white blood cell (right) attacks pathogens. The colours were added to the photo.

author: Yale Rosen from USA
caption: Lung tissue under a microscope: the white spaces are air sacs, and their walls are very thin and full of tiny red blood cells in capillaries.

author: Krishna satya 333
caption: A fish gill: hundreds of thin, red filaments full of blood vessels give a big surface for oxygen to pass from the water into the blood.

author: reosarevok
caption: An Anopheles mosquito — the insect vector that carries the malaria parasite from one person to another.

author: Ajay Kumar Chaurasiya
caption: Bacteria growing on an agar plate: each separate round spot is a colony that grew from bacteria put on the jelly.

author: Alexis Lours
caption: The cattle egret, a common bird in Egyptian fields, eats grasshoppers and other insects — so it is a secondary consumer.

author: Luc Viatour
caption: A barn owl hunting: it eats many mice, so it can build up a large amount of any toxic pesticide the mice have taken in.

author: James St. John
caption: Mercury is a metal, but at room temperature it is a shiny liquid, because its melting point (−39 °C) is below room temperature.

author: Petar Milošević
caption: Inside an electrical cable: copper wires (electrical conductors) are each covered in plastic (an electrical insulator).

author: Helen Owl
caption: Salt crystals left behind where salty lake water evaporated — the dissolved salt is back as a solid, so dissolving is reversible.

author: Дарья Могилевцева
caption: Blue copper sulfate crystals that formed as water evaporated from copper sulfate solution — the same substance comes back.

author: Markus Schweiss
caption: Water boiling: big bubbles of water vapour form all through the liquid, not only at the surface.

author: NASA
caption: Salt evaporation ponds south of the Dead Sea, photographed from the International Space Station: wide, shallow ponds give a large surface area, so water evaporates quickly.

author: Nicole López
caption: Drops of condensation on cold glass: water vapour from the air cooled and turned back into liquid water.

author: Dr.T
caption: Magnesium reacting with hydrochloric acid: the bubbles are a new gas (hydrogen), evidence of a chemical reaction.

author: W.carter
caption: A rusty iron chain: iron reacted with oxygen and water to make orange-brown rust, a new substance.
